primary_concerns: Server scalability under high user load
mitigated_by_design: HTTP polling fallback reduces WebSocket complexity
Existing JWT auth reduces new security surface

frontend_risks.impact: Chat feature may not work reliably, crashes possible
frontend_risks.description: JUCE does not have built-in WebSocket support. We would need to either implement the WebSocket protocol manually using juce::StreamingSocket or integrate an external library.
mitigation: MVP approach: Use HTTP polling instead of WebSocket (poll every 2-3 seconds)
Alternative: Integrate websocketpp library via CMake
Alternative: Use JUCE's juce::URL::InputStream for simple REST calls only
frontend_risks.recommendation: Start with HTTP polling for MVP. Add WebSocket in Phase 2 if needed.

frontend_risks.risk: Message list performance with many messages
frontend_risks.impact: UI lag when scrolling through hundreds of messages
frontend_risks.description: If users keep ChatPage open for extended periods, the message list may grow large and cause rendering slowdowns.
mitigation: Limit displayed messages to last 100, with 'Load More' button
Use juce::Viewport with virtual scrolling (only render visible items)
Clear old messages when count exceeds threshold
frontend_risks.recommendation: Implement virtual scrolling from the start

frontend_risks.impact: App appears unresponsive during connection/message loading
frontend_risks.description: Network operations blocking the JUCE message thread will freeze the UI.
mitigation: All network calls MUST be on background thread
Use juce::MessageManager::callAsync() to update UI from background
Add timeout handling for slow connections
frontend_risks.recommendation: Follow existing SAMPLAR patterns for async operations (see ProcessingPage)

frontend_risks.impact: Users unsure if they're connected or if messages are sending
frontend_risks.description: Without clear connection status indicators, users may be confused when offline or experiencing lag.
mitigation: Always show connection status indicator (green/red dot)
Show 'Sending...' state for outgoing messages
Auto-reconnect with visual feedback

frontend_risks.impact: Malicious message text could potentially cause display issues
frontend_risks.description: While JUCE is not a web browser, special characters or extremely long messages could cause display problems.
mitigation: Sanitize displayed text (escape special characters)
Limit message display length with ellipsis
Validate message text on server side

backend_risks.risk: Server overload with many concurrent WebSocket connections
backend_risks.impact: Server becomes unresponsive, chat stops working for all users
backend_risks.description: Each WebSocket connection consumes server resources. With many concurrent users, the single Render.com instance may be overwhelmed.
mitigation: Implement connection limits per server instance
Monitor connection count and add alerts
Design for horizontal scaling (Redis pubsub for multi-instance)
HTTP polling as fallback uses less persistent resources
backend_risks.recommendation: Start with HTTP polling for MVP, add WebSocket later with proper scaling

backend_risks.description: If JWT tokens are intercepted, attackers could use them to send messages as other users.
mitigation: Use HTTPS only (already in place)
Short token expiration (15 minutes)
Validate token signature on every message
Add token refresh mechanism
backend_risks.recommendation: Rely on existing license server JWT security, add validation on every request

backend_risks.impact: Toxic environment drives away users, potential legal issues
backend_risks.description: Public chat rooms are vulnerable to spam, hate speech, and inappropriate content.
mitigation: Implement word filter for obvious profanity
Add report button for users to flag messages
Admin tools to ban users and delete messages
Rate limiting prevents spam floods
backend_risks.recommendation: MVP: Rate limiting + basic word filter. Phase 2: Report system + admin tools

backend_risks.impact: Database queries slow down, storage costs increase
backend_risks.description: Without cleanup, chat_messages table will grow indefinitely.
mitigation: Implement message retention policy (delete messages older than 30 days)
Create cleanup job that runs daily
Proper indexing for efficient queries

backend_risks.risk: Chat service brings down license server
backend_risks.impact: License validation stops working, affecting all users
backend_risks.description: If chat_service plugin causes crashes or high CPU, it could affect critical license operations.
mitigation: Isolate chat operations with try/catch
Separate database connection pool for chat
Monitor chat service health independently
backend_risks.recommendation: Design chat plugin to be independently restartable

backend_risks.description: Malicious message content could attempt SQL injection.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries (already standard in database_manager)
Validate and sanitize all input
Limit message length (1000 characters max)

integration_risks.impact: Users lose access to existing community features
integration_risks.description: Replacing CommunityPage with ChatPage might break existing navigation or features.
mitigation: Option A: Keep both pages, add new ChatPage at index 8
Option B: Replace CommunityPage but keep WebBrowser as tab in ChatPage
Test all navigation paths after changes
integration_risks.recommendation: Add ChatPage as NEW page (index 8), keep CommunityPage working

integration_risks.risk: Auth token not available when user opens chat
integration_risks.impact: Users cannot use chat until they sign in separately
integration_risks.description: Some users may not have authenticated with the license server yet.
mitigation: Check auth status when ChatPage opens
Show 'Sign In' button if not authenticated
Redirect to license activation if needed
integration_risks.recommendation: Handle unauthenticated state gracefully with clear UI

integration_risks.risk: Server and client out of sync during deployment
integration_risks.impact: Old clients fail to connect to new server API
integration_risks.description: If API changes, older SAMPLAR builds may fail to work with new server.
mitigation: Version the API (/api/v1/chat/...)
Maintain backwards compatibility for at least one version
Return clear error messages for unsupported clients
integration_risks.recommendation: Use versioned API from the start

high_priority: FE-001: WebSocket complexity -> Use HTTP polling for MVP
BE-003: Content moderation -> Rate limiting + word filter
INT-002: Auth not available -> Handle gracefully in UI
medium_priority: FE-003: UI freezes -> Background thread for all network
BE-001: Server scalability -> Design for scaling, start simple
BE-002: JWT security -> Validate on every request
low_priority: FE-002: Message list performance -> Virtual scrolling

rollback_plan.description: If chat feature causes critical issues, how to roll back
steps: 1. Server: Disable chat_service plugin by removing from load list
2. Client: Next release removes ChatPage, restores COMMUNITY button to CommunityPage
3. Database: Keep chat_messages table but stop writing to it
rollback_plan.recovery_time: Server: 5 minutes (config change + restart). Client: Next release cycle.

scenarios.expected: Message shows in list within 1 second
Message appears for User B within 3 seconds
Chat reconnects automatically, shows missed messages
Error message after 10th message, messages resume after cooldown
Shows 'Sign In' button, does not crash
Last 50 messages visible, loading indicator shown during fetch

conditions: Use HTTP polling instead of WebSocket for MVP to reduce complexity
Add ChatPage as NEW page (index 8), do not remove CommunityPage
Implement rate limiting and basic word filter before release
